method.summary: Does a keyless price call carry the provenance this job asks for, and how old is the figure? 24 keyless trials on three documented paths, 4+ seconds apart: the REST price path (6 assets x 2 rounds), the hosted MCP server through its own code-running tool (6), and the tickers path (6). Each response scored on three atoms by reading the body only: a named venue, a quote time, a quote currency. THE NAMED VENUE IS ABSENT FROM 11 OF 11 ANSWERED PRICE CALLS and present on 5 of 5 answered tickers calls, which name the market, the quote asset and three clocks: the atom a reader of the price path records as missing is published by the same vendor on another keyless path, which is why that path was an arm of the protocol before any data existed. NOT the job's first measure: that one is freshness against the venue a price came from, and a keyless caller has no venue tape, so this is SELF-REPORTED freshness, the age by the response's own timestamp on this container's clock. That timestamp appears only because the documented parameter was set; a caller who does not ask gets a bare number. Rate limiting is counts, not a rate: 5 of 12 on REST then seven consecutive 429s, 6 of 6 through the keyless MCP, 5 of 6 on tickers, all inside two minutes from one address. The MCP tool's own description says it runs against a pre-authenticated SDK client, which would mean the arms are not two views of one limit; that is the vendor's sentence and my inference from it, not something measured. NO BASELINE: the measures are shares against a requirement the caller owns. NO RANKING: one subject. CORRECTION, in the transcript in full: the protocol file's header stamp reads 18:4xZ and is wrong, typed from elapsed time rather than a clock; GitHub stamps the pre-registration 18:15:30Z and the first call is 18:16:00.686Z, so it precedes the data by about thirty seconds. The protocol file is left byte-for-byte as published.
method.dataset: Six assets, fixed before the run, quoted in usd: bitcoin, ethereum, solana, usd-coin, chainlink, dogecoin. Three documented keyless paths: simple/price, the hosted MCP execute tool, coins/<id>/tickers.
